It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) belonging to the desire realm, as well as their associated and other such dharmas; these are called causes that are not yet abandoned, and those that are already abandoned, whose essential nature has been severed.
Regarding all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm: if their substance has not been abandoned, does that which is un-abandoned serve as their cause?
Answer: It is so.
If that which has not been abandoned serves as the cause, is its substance also not abandoned?
Or, that which has not been abandoned serves as the cause and its substance is not abandoned;
or, both that which has not been abandoned and that which has already been abandoned serve as the cause, and its substance has already been abandoned.

"Having non-abandonment as its cause while its substance is not yet abandoned" refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm belonging to individuals who are still bound by all fetters; this is called "having non-abandonment as its cause while its substance is not yet abandoned."

Regarding those that have the un-abandoned as their cause and those that have the already-abandoned as their cause, the entity that has already been abandoned refers to one who has not yet abandoned the craving of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

When the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, what is the "already-abandoned cause" for the obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds associated with the desire realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

It refers to the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) within the desire realm, as well as their associated and other such dharmas; these are called "having what has not yet been abandoned as their cause," while those whose essence has already been abandoned are called "having what has already been abandoned as their cause."

Regarding all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta-anivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*): if their substance has not been severed, does that which is not severed serve as their cause?

Excluding those results of maturation (*vipāka*) produced by the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*), regarding the remaining unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm: if their substance has not been severed, does that which is not severed serve as their cause?
He said: "It is so. If that which has not been abandoned serves as a cause, does its substance remain unabandoned?
He replied:
It is so. Regarding the maturation (vipāka) produced by the various underlying tendencies (anuśaya), either their substance has not been abandoned and thus they act as an un-abandoned cause;
or their substance has not been abandoned, yet they act as both an abandoned cause and an un-abandoned cause.

Regarding those whose substance has not been severed and which take what has not been severed as their cause: this refers to the various resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) of a person bound by all fetters; or, for one who has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of sensuality, the resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as through cultivation, once the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen.

The various resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and through cultivation, when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen;

and the various resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions to be abandoned through the vision of the path and through cultivation, when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.

If one observes the resultant matured minds (*vipākacitta*) produced by the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation, belonging to a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm—this is called "the entity is not yet severed, with that which is not yet severed as its cause."
Regarding "those whose substance has not been severed, which have both already-severed and not-yet-severed as their causes": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm.

When the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are various resultant consciousnesses (*vipākacitta*) produced by the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering. What are their not-yet-severed causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

It refers to the various proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipāka-citta*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, regarding the various resultant consciousnesses produced by the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination: what are their unsevered causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

It refers to the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin, which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipāka-citta*).

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, regarding the various resultant consciousnesses produced by the latent dispositions (anuśaya) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent and associated dharmas and so forth.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

It refers to the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) and so forth, abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipākacitta*).

If one considers the resultant consciousnesses produced by the latent tendencies to be abandoned through seeing, belonging to a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of sensuality: what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the factors that coexist with and are associated [with it], and so forth.
What are the causes that have already been abandoned?
They are the various proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-heya*), which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipāka-citta*).
This is called "the entity is not yet severed, [yet] that which is already severed serves as its cause and that which is not yet severed also serves as its cause.
If that which is not yet severed serves as its cause, is the entity itself not yet severed?
He replied:
Thus it is. Regarding wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), if their substance has not been severed, does that which is not yet severed serve as their cause?
He replied:
Thus it is. If that which has not been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance also not abandoned?
He replied:

It is so. Regarding those minds associated with the form realm that are obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*): if their substance has not been abandoned, do they have what is un-abandoned as their cause? Or rather, if their substance has not been abandoned, they have what is un-abandoned as their cause;
[and conversely,] if they have what is un-abandoned as their cause, their substance has not been abandoned.
Alternatively, there are cases where the entity is not yet abandoned, and it has both that which is already abandoned as its cause and that which is not yet abandoned as its cause.

Regarding those cases where the entity is not yet abandoned and has only that which is not yet abandoned as its cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm belonging to a *pudgala* who is bound by all fetters; specifically, for one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, these obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm are called "entities not yet abandoned having only that which is not yet abandoned as their cause."

Regarding "those whose substance has not been abandoned, which have both already-abandoned and not-yet-abandoned as their causes": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen. For such a person, what are the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm that are abandoned through seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation? What are their not-yet-abandoned causes?
This refers to the coexistent, associated, and other such factors.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering within the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), as well as their associated and other such factors.

When the subsequent knowledge of origination (*anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*anvaya-nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, for those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation, the path, or cultivation—what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent and associated dharmas, etc.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) and their associated dharmas, etc.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, for those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) of the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision and cultivation paths, what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such factors.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as their associated and other such factors.

If one observes a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, what are the unabandoned causes of their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the realm of form?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such factors.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as their associated and other such factors.
This is called "the entity is not yet severed, [having] that which is already severed as its cause and that which is not yet severed as its cause.
If it has that which is not yet severed as its cause, is its entity not yet severed?

Or, having that which is not yet severed as its cause while its entity is not yet severed; or, having both that which is not yet severed and that which is already severed as its causes while its entity is not yet severed; or, having both that which is not yet severed and that which is already severed as its causes while its entity is already severed.

"Having non-abandonment as its cause, while its own substance is not yet abandoned" refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm belonging to a person who is bound by all fetters; specifically, for one who has already abandoned desire for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned desire for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, these obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm are called "having non-abandonment as their cause, while their own substance is not yet abandoned."

Regarding that which has not been abandoned as its cause, both that which has not yet been abandoned and that which has already been abandoned, but whose substance has not yet been abandoned: this refers to one who has not yet detached from the greed of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen. For such a person, all minds associated with the form realm that are obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*)—whether abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, or the path, or abandoned through cultivation—what are their causes that have not yet been abandoned?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such factors.
What are the causes that have already been abandoned?

They are the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) belonging to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as their associated and other such factors.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, for those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, or by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), as well as their associated and other such dharmas.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, for those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) belonging to the form realm that are to be abandoned through the path of seeing and the path of cultivation, what are the causes that have not yet been severed?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such factors.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as their associated and other such factors.

If one considers a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, what are the unsevered causes of their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the realm of form that are to be abandoned through cultivation?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), as well as their associated and other such dharmas.
This is called that which has both the unsevered and the severed as its causes, yet its substance is not severed.

Regarding that which has both the unsevered and the severed as its causes and whose substance is already severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified mind associated with the form realm that has not been severed by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana*), occurring when one has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaye ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen. What are its severed causes?
This refers to the coexistent and associated dharmas and so forth.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) which are bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as their associated dharmas and so forth.
This is called that which has both the unsevered as its cause and the severed as its cause, yet whose own substance is already severed.

Regarding those minds associated with the form realm (rūpadhātu) that are non-obscured and indeterminate (anivṛtāvyākṛta): if their substance is not yet severed, do they have the unsevered as their cause?
He said: "It is so.
If that which has not been abandoned serves as a cause, does its substance remain unabandoned?"
He said: "It is so.
Regarding those wholesome minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), if their substance has not been severed, do they have as their cause that which is not yet severed?"
He said: "It is so.
If that which has not been abandoned serves as a cause, does its substance remain unabandoned?"
He said: "It is so.
Regarding the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm, if their substance has not been severed, do they take what is not yet severed as their cause?"

Either its substance is not yet abandoned and has non-abandonment as its cause, or its substance is not yet abandoned and has both abandonment and non-abandonment as its causes. Regarding those whose substance is not yet abandoned and have non-abandonment as their cause:

this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm belonging to a person who is bound by all fetters; or the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm belonging to one who has already abandoned desire for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned desire for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

or the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm belonging to one who has already abandoned desire for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering has not yet arisen.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, and what is not yet abandoned serves as its cause.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned where both what is already abandoned and what is not yet abandoned serve as causes: this refers to the mind associated with the formless realm that is bound by views regarding the origin, cessation, and path, as well as the obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through cultivation, at a time when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) belonging to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), as well as the associated and co-arising dharmas.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, what are the unabandoned causes for the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) belonging to the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*)?
This refers to the co-existent and associated dharmas [of that mind].
What are the causes that have already been abandoned?
They are the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated and co-existent dharmas.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, regarding the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the path of seeing and cultivation, what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the coexistent and associated dharmas and so forth.
What are the causes that have been abandoned?
They are the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated dharmas and so forth.

If one considers a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, what are the unsevered causes of their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such factors.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) bound to the formless realm and their associated, and other such factors.
This is called that whose substance is not yet abandoned, having both what is already abandoned as its cause and what is not yet abandoned as its cause.
If it has what is not yet abandoned as its cause, is its substance not yet abandoned?

Or is it the case that when it has what is not yet abandoned as its cause, its substance is not yet abandoned; or when it has what is not yet abandoned as its cause and what is already abandoned as its cause, its substance is not yet abandoned; or when it has what is not yet abandoned as its cause and what is already abandoned as its cause, its substance is already abandoned?

Regarding those whose nature has not been severed because their cause has not been severed: this refers to (1) individuals bound by all fetters, and their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm;

(2) those who have already abandoned desire for the desire realm but have not yet abandoned desire for the form realm, and whose subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, and their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm;

and (3) those who have already abandoned desire for the form realm but whose subsequent knowledge of suffering has not yet arisen, and their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm.
This is called that which has non-abandonment as its cause and whose substance is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has both non-abandonment as its cause and abandonment as its cause, yet whose substance is not yet abandoned: this refers to the minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation—specifically, when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen. These are the obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds.
What is the cause that has not been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) pertaining to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), as well as the associated dharmas and so forth.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, regarding the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) pertaining to the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, or through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*), what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated and other such dharmas.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, regarding those obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the path of seeing and the path of cultivation, what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the co-existent, associated, and other such dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated and other such dharmas.

If one observes a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, what are the unsevered causes of their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through cultivation?
This refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated factors.
This is called that which has both the unsevered and the severed as its cause, yet whose substance is unsevered;

and that which has both the unsevered and the severed as its cause, yet whose substance is severed. Regarding the latter: when the knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, it refers to the obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) associated with the formless realm (ārūpyadhātu) that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

That is to say: the universal underlying tendencies (anuśaya) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) that are bound to the formless realm (ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta), along with their associated dharmas and so forth;
and all unobscured-neutral minds (anivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) bound to the formless realm—if their substance has not yet been abandoned, do they have what has not yet been abandoned as their cause?
He said: "It is so.
If that which has not been abandoned serves as a cause, does its substance remain unabandoned?"
It is said:
So it is. *Sarvāstivāda-vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra*, Fascicle Four.
The Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra, Chapter Five,
composed by the Arhat Devaśarman;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.

2. The Second Part of the Third Aggregate on the Causes and Conditions of the Uddāna Verses: There are ten types of mind, namely: wholesome mind, unwholesome mind, obscured-neutral mind, and non-obscured-neutral mind bound to the desire realm; wholesome mind, obscured-neutral mind, and non-obscured-neutral mind bound to the form realm; and wholesome mind, obscured-neutral mind, and non-obscured-neutral mind bound to the formless realm.
Regarding those wholesome minds bound to the desire realm: if their substance has already been severed, have they already been severed as causes?
Conversely, if they have already been severed as causes, has their substance already been severed?

Up to the unobscured-neutral mind associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta-ani-vṛtāvyākṛta-citta*): if its substance has already been severed, is that which has been severed the cause?
Or, if that which has been severed is the cause, has its substance already been severed?
Regarding all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), if their substance has already been severed, have those that are severed served as causes? Answer: It is so.
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, has its own substance already been abandoned?
It is said: Yes.
Regarding all unwholesome minds: if their substance has already been severed, is that which is severed the cause?
Either their substance has been severed and that which is severed is the cause;
or their substance has been severed, and both that which is severed and that which is not yet severed are the causes.

Regarding those whose substance has already been severed and which take what is already severed as their cause: this refers to unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin for one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, when the knowledge of origin has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen;
and unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering, its origin, and its cessation, when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.

If one considers the unwholesome minds of a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One who has fully realized the vision [of the truths]: those unwholesome minds that have not yet abandoned the craving of the desire realm;
those unwholesome minds that have already abandoned the craving of the desire realm but have not yet abandoned the craving of the form realm;

those unwholesome minds that have already abandoned the craving of the form realm but have not yet abandoned the craving of the formless realm; and those unwholesome minds that have already abandoned the craving of the formless realm—these are called "the substance having been abandoned, and being abandoned, serving as the cause."

Regarding those whose substance has already been severed, yet for which both that which is already severed and that which is not yet severed serve as causes: this refers to unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering, belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, in whom the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors such as the co-existent and associated dharmas.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the desire realm, as well as the factors associated with them and so forth.
These are said to have their substance already abandoned, and thus to have both what is already abandoned and what is not yet abandoned as their causes.
If that which has been abandoned serves as the cause, is its substance already abandoned?

Is it the case that when something has been abandoned as the cause, its substance is already abandoned; or that when something has been abandoned as the cause and something not yet abandoned also serves as the cause, its substance is already abandoned; or that when both something abandoned and something not yet abandoned serve as causes, its substance is not yet abandoned?

Regarding those whose nature has already been severed because they have already been severed as causes: this refers to the unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin for one who has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire—specifically when the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

and the unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering, its origin, and its cessation—specifically when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
If one observes the unwholesome minds that are to be abandoned by insight belonging to a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but is not yet free from craving for the desire realm;
or those belonging to one who is already free from craving for the desire realm but not yet free from craving for the form realm;

or those belonging to one who is already free from craving for the form realm but not yet free from craving for the formless realm; or those belonging to one who is already free from craving for the formless realm—these are called "having been severed as their cause, while their substance is already severed."

Regarding those whose nature has already been abandoned, yet which have both the abandoned and the unabandoned as their causes: this refers to the unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering, belonging to one who has not yet detached from the craving of the desire realm, for whom the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the desire realm, as well as the factors associated with them and so forth.
These are called those whose substance has already been abandoned, yet which serve as causes both for what is already abandoned and for what is not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose causes have been severed as well as those whose causes have not yet been severed, yet whose essential nature has not been severed: this refers to the various unwholesome minds of one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; these include the minds associated with the views of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent, associated, and so forth with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), along with their associated and co-arising factors;

as well as all unwholesome minds to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*), at a time when the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent, associated, and so forth with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (anuśaya) bound to the desire realm and their associated dharmas;

as well as the unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of seeing and the path of cultivation, at a time when the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (anuśaya) bound to the desire realm and their associated dharmas,

as well as the unwholesome minds of a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, which are to be abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya).
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (anuśaya) bound to the desire realm and their associated dharmas; these are called "having been abandoned as causes" while "not having been abandoned as causes," because their essential substance has not yet been severed.
Regarding those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*): if their substance has already been abandoned, is that which is abandoned the cause?

Either their substance has already been abandoned and that which is abandoned is the cause, or their substance has already been abandoned and both that which is abandoned and that which is not yet abandoned are the causes.

Regarding those whose substance has already been severed and which take what is already severed as their cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm for one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen;
and the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.
If one observes a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, there are all the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm;
or one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, there are all the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm;
or one who has already abandoned craving for the form realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, there are all the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the desire realm.

Those obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the desire realm that have already abandoned craving for the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) are said to have their substance already severed and to have what is already severed as their cause.

Those whose substance has both what is already severed and what is not yet severed as their causes refer to those who have not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; these are the obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the desire realm, as well as the factors associated with them and so forth; these are termed "having their substance already abandoned" while "acting as causes both for what is already abandoned and for what is not yet abandoned."
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance itself already abandoned? Answer: It is so.
Regarding all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm: if their substance has already been severed, have they already been severed as causes?
Answer: It is so.
If that which has already been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance also already abandoned?
This refers to the non-obscured, neutral minds associated with the desire realm, excluding the maturation resulting from latent dispositions (*anuśaya*).
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance also abandoned? Answer: It is so.

Regarding the various resultant minds produced by latent dispositions (*anuśaya*), either they have their cause already abandoned while their substance is already abandoned, or they have their cause already abandoned while their substance is not yet abandoned, due to causes that are both already abandoned and not yet abandoned.

"Having been severed as its cause, yet its substance is already severed" refers to: the various resultant minds produced by latent dispositions (anuśaya) for one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm;
the various resultant minds produced by latent dispositions for one who has already abandoned craving for the form realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm;

and the various resultant minds produced by latent dispositions for one who has already abandoned craving for the formless realm. These are termed "having been severed as its cause, yet its substance is already severed."

Regarding those whose cause has been severed and whose cause has not yet been severed, yet whose substance has not been severed: this refers to the various resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions (anuśaya) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, belonging to one who has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire, in whom the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) and so forth to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipāka-citta*).

It also refers to the resultant consciousnesses produced by the latent dispositions to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin (*samudaya*), [at a time] when the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are coexistent, associated, and so forth with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin, which are capable of producing such resultant minds (*vipākacitta*).

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, regarding the resultant minds produced by the latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of suffering, its origin, and its cessation, what are their unsevered causes?
This refers to the co-existent and associated dharmas and so forth.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

It refers to the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, which are capable of producing such resultant consciousnesses (*vipākacitta*).

If one considers the resultant consciousnesses produced by the latent dispositions (anuśaya) to be abandoned through insight, belonging to a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of sensuality—
what are their unabandoned causes?
This refers to the coexistent and associated dharmas and so forth.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

It refers to the various proclivities (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-heya*), which can induce such resultant consciousnesses (*vipāka-citta*); these are called causes that have already been abandoned, as well as causes that have not yet been abandoned because their substance has not yet been severed.
Regarding all wholesome minds bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), if their substance has already been severed, have those that are severed served as causes? Answer: It is so.
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance already abandoned? Answer: It is so.

Regarding all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*): if their substance has already been abandoned, are they caused by what has already been abandoned?

Either their substance has already been abandoned and they are caused by what has already been abandoned, or their substance has already been abandoned and they are caused both by what has already been abandoned and by what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding those whose substance has already been severed and which have that severance as their cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of origin, occurring when one has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, at the stage when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudayānvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

and the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, the vision of origin, and the vision of cessation, occurring when the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

If one considers a perfected disciple of the World-Honored One who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), their obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛtacitta*) associated with the realm of form that are to be abandoned by insight;

or one who has already abandoned craving for the realm of form but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the realm of form;

or one who has already abandoned craving for the formless realm, their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the realm of form—these are called "the entity is already abandoned, and what is abandoned serves as its cause."

Regarding that which has already been abandoned and takes both what has already been abandoned and what has not yet been abandoned as its cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified mind associated with the form realm that is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, at a time when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as the factors associated with them and so forth; these are called "those whose substance has already been abandoned, which have both already-abandoned and not-yet-abandoned factors as their causes."
If that which has been abandoned serves as the cause, is its substance already abandoned?

Or does it occur such that (1) that which has been abandoned serves as the cause and its substance is already abandoned; or (2) that which has been abandoned and that which has not yet been abandoned serve as the causes and its substance is already abandoned; or (3) that which has been abandoned and that which has not yet been abandoned serve as the causes and its substance is not yet abandoned?

Regarding "that which has already been abandoned as its cause, while its own substance has already been abandoned": this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of origin, belonging to those who have not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, at the stage when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛta-avyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm (*rūpa-dhātu*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation.

Furthermore, for a disciple of the Blessed One who is perfected in vision but has not yet abandoned desire for the form realm, there are the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm to be abandoned by vision;

and for one who has already abandoned desire for the form realm but has not yet abandoned desire for the formless realm (*ārūpya-dhātu*), there are the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm.

The obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) of one who has already abandoned craving for the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-tṛṣṇā*) are called "those whose cause has been severed and whose substance is already severed.

Regarding those "whose cause has been severed" and "whose cause has not been severed, yet whose substance is already severed," this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds bound to the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), occurring when one has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as the factors associated with them and so forth; these are called those whose substance has been abandoned, yet which act as causes both for what has already been abandoned and for what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding those whose nature is not yet severed, having both that which is already severed as their cause and that which is not yet severed as their cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation, for one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) pertaining to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), along with their associated and co-arising factors;

and, when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) pertaining to the form realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the form realm and their associated dharmas;

specifically, when the knowledge of the cessation of categories (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) has arisen but the knowledge of the path of categories (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, it pertains to the obscured-unspecified (nivṛtāvyākṛta) minds of the form realm that are to be abandoned through the path of vision (darśana-mārga) and cultivation (bhāvanā-mārga).
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors such as the coexistent and associated dharmas.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the form realm and their associated dharmas;

as well as, for a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, the obscured-unspecified minds that are to be abandoned through cultivation and are bound to the form realm.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it, and so forth.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the realm of form (rūpadhātu) and their associated dharmas;
these are called those whose substance is not yet abandoned, even though they function as causes both for what has already been abandoned and for what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta-ani-vṛtāvyākṛta-citta*): if their substance has already been abandoned, have they already been abandoned as causes?
Answer: It is so.
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance also already abandoned?
It is said: so it is.
Regarding all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm: if their substance has already been severed, have those that are severed served as causes?
Answer: It is so.
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance itself already abandoned?
It is said: Yes.

Regarding all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*): if their substance has already been abandoned, are they caused by what has already been abandoned?

Either their substance has already been abandoned and they are caused by what has already been abandoned, or their substance has already been abandoned and they are caused both by what has already been abandoned and by what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding those whose substance has already been abandoned and which have abandonment as their cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of origin, occurring when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

and it refers to the unobscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, the vision of origin, and the vision of cessation, occurring when the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

If one considers a perfected disciple of the World-Honored One who has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, there are all the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned by insight;
or, if they have already abandoned craving for the formless realm, there are all the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm.
This is called "having its substance already abandoned, with that which is already abandoned as its cause.

Regarding that which has its substance already abandoned, with both what is already abandoned and what is not yet abandoned as its cause: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, at a time when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the universal underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as the factors associated with them and so forth.
These are called "those whose substance has already been abandoned, which have both the already-abandoned and the not-yet-abandoned as their causes."
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance already abandoned?

Or does it occur such that when that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, its substance is already abandoned; or when both that which has been abandoned and that which has not yet been abandoned serve as causes, its substance is already abandoned; or when both that which has been abandoned and that which has not yet been abandoned serve as causes, its substance is not yet abandoned?

Regarding those whose nature has already been severed and which act as causes for what is already severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and the vision of origin—occurring when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

and the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, the vision of origin, and the vision of cessation—occurring when the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

If one sees the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned by insight belonging to a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm;
or the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm belonging to one who has already abandoned craving for the formless realm.
This is called that which has already been abandoned as its cause, while its own substance has already been abandoned.

Regarding that which has already been abandoned as its cause and also has not yet been abandoned as its cause, while its own substance has already been abandoned: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, at a time when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
It refers to those factors such as the co-existent and associated dharmas.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?

This refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that are bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), as well as the factors associated with them and so forth.
These are called those whose substance has been abandoned, yet which serve as causes both for what has already been abandoned and for what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding those whose causes have already been severed and whose causes have not yet been severed, while their own substance has not yet been severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation, at a time when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?

This refers to the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) pertaining to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), along with their associated and co-arising factors;

and, when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, the obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds pertaining to the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).
What is the cause that has not been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the pervasive latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated dharmas;

as well as the obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) bound to the formless realm that are to be abandoned through the path of seeing and cultivation, at the stage when the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen.
What is the cause that has not yet been abandoned?
It refers to those dharmas that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal proclivities (sarvatraga-anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated factors,

as well as the obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya) belonging to the formless realm, which arise in a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm.
What is the cause that has not been abandoned?
It refers to those factors that are co-existent and associated with it.
What is the cause that has already been abandoned?
This refers to the universal latent dispositions (anuśaya) bound to the formless realm and their associated dharmas;
these are called those whose nature is not yet abandoned, even though they act as causes for what has already been abandoned and for what has not yet been abandoned.

Regarding those non-obscured neutral minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), if their substance has already been severed, have they already ceased to serve as causes? Answer: It is so.
If that which has been abandoned serves as a cause, is its substance itself already abandoned? Answer: It is so.
There are fifteen types of consciousness: namely, five types of consciousness bound to the desire realm, five types bound to the form realm, and five types bound to the formless realm.
These fifteen types of consciousness are either past, future, or present.
What are the five types of mind associated with the desire realm? They are:

the mind associated with the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering; and the minds associated with the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as through cultivation.
As it is for the desire realm, so it is for the form realm and the formless realm.

Regarding the latent dispositions (anuśaya) associated with the past mind of the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), if they increase in accordance with (*anuśerate*) this mind, are they also its cause (*hetu*)?
If they are established as causes, do they also increase accordingly?

Furthermore, regarding all latent dispositions (anuśaya) associated with the past mind of the formless realm that is abandoned through cultivation—do those which increase accordingly toward this mind also act as its cause?
If it is established as a cause, is it also a point of increase?

Regarding all the latent dispositions (anuśaya) present in a past mind of the desire realm that is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), if they are points of increase for that mind, are they also its causes?

Either it can serve as a cause but is not an object of increase, or it is an object of increase but cannot serve as a cause, or it can serve as a cause and is also an object of increase, or it cannot serve as a cause and is also not an object of increase.

Furthermore, regarding those that can act as causes but do not increase through association: this refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) of the same class or universal types that preceded this mind; specifically, those latent dispositions which do not take this [mind] as their object, or which, even if they did take it as an object, have already been abandoned, as well as the associated latent dispositions that have already been abandoned.

Regarding those that increase concomitantly [with a mind] yet cannot serve as its cause: this refers to those underlying tendencies (anuśaya) which, being of the same class or universal in nature, arise after this mind and have not yet been abandoned, while taking this very mind as their object.

That which can act as a cause and is also subject to increase through association refers to those proclivities that, being of the same class and universal, precede this mind; that is, those proclivities which take this [mind] as their object and have not yet been abandoned, as well as the proclivities associated with it that have not yet been abandoned.

That which cannot serve as a cause and does not increase by way of being an object (*anuśerate*) refers to those latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that are of the same class or are universal (*sarvatraga*) occurring after this mind; specifically, those dispositions which do not take this [mind] as their object, or which have been abandoned even if they once did, or those that take other objects, or other latent dispositions, or universal latent dispositions belonging to a different realm (*dhātu*).

Just as it is with the past mind associated with the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), so it is with the future mind associated with the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering.

Regarding all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) present in the current mind associated with the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering: do those which increase in accordance with (*anuśerate*) this mind also act as its cause?

There are cases where something can act as a cause but is not an object of increase; cases where it is an object of increase but cannot act as a cause; cases where it can act as a cause and is also an object of increase; and cases where it neither acts as a cause nor is an object of increase.

Furthermore, regarding those that can serve as causes but do not increase through association: this refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) of the same class or universal types that preceded this mind; specifically, those dispositions which do not take this [mind] as their object, or which, though they once did, have already been abandoned.

Regarding those that increase along with it but cannot act as a cause: this refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) which, being of the same class or universally pervasive, follow after this mind, and those very latent dispositions take this [mind] as their object and have not yet been abandoned.

That which can both act as a cause and be subject to increase through association refers to those proclivities that, being of the same class and universal, precede this mind; specifically, those proclivities that take this [mind] as their object and have not yet been abandoned, as well as all proclivities associated with it.

That which cannot serve as a cause and is not subject to subsequent increase refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) that, being of the same class or universal, follow after this mind; specifically, those latent dispositions which do not take this [mind] as their object, or which, though taking it as an object, have already been abandoned, or which take other objects, or which are other latent dispositions, or which are universal latent dispositions belonging to a different realm.

As it is with the mind abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), so it is with the defiled minds abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).

Regarding the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that exist within a past, desire-realm-bound, non-defiled mind abandoned through cultivation: do they both increase in accordance with that mind and also act as its cause?

This refers to the latent dispositions (anuśaya) belonging to all past, desire-realm-bound, non-defiled minds abandoned through cultivation, excluding those that are the maturation (vipāka) resulting from latent dispositions; if these latent dispositions increase in accordance with this mind, they do not act as its cause.
If something can serve as a cause for this mind, it is neither an underlying tendency (*anuśaya*) nor does it increase along with it (*anuśerate*).

Regarding the resultant mind produced by an underlying tendency, there are four possibilities: that which can serve as a cause but does not increase along with it; that which increases along with it but cannot serve as a cause; that which can serve as a cause and also increases along with it; or that which cannot serve as a cause and also does not increase along with it.

Furthermore, regarding that which can serve as a cause but does not increase through association: this refers to those latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that, acting as causes, bring about the maturation (*vipāka*) of this mind; yet, those very latent dispositions do not take this [mind] as their object, or if they do take it as their object, they have already been abandoned.

Regarding those that increase along with [the mind] but cannot act as its cause: this refers to those latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) which do not act as the cause for the maturation (*vipāka*) of this mind, yet those very dispositions take this mind as their object and have not been abandoned.

That which is both a cause and that which increases through association refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) that, acting as causes, bring about the maturation (vipāka) of this mind, and those very same latent dispositions for which this [mind] has not yet been abandoned as an object-condition (ālambana).

That which cannot act as a cause and does not increase by way of being an object-condition refers to those latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that do not serve as causes for the maturation (*vipāka*) of this mind; that is, those very latent dispositions which do not take this [mind] as their object, or which have been abandoned even if they once took it as an object, or other objects, or other latent dispositions, or universal latent dispositions belonging to a different realm.
As it is with the past, so it is with the future and the present.

As it is with that which is bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), so it is with that which is bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*).

In this context, there is a distinction: one should not say that there is the maturation (*vipāka*) of latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) for minds bound to the form realm or minds bound to the formless realm.
There are fifteen states of mind: namely, five states of mind bound to the desire realm, five states of mind bound to the form realm, and five states of mind bound to the formless realm.
These fifteen states of mind are either past, future, or present.
What are the five types of minds associated with the desire realm? They are:

the mind associated with the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering; and the minds associated with the desire realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as through cultivation.
As it is for those associated with the desire realm, so it is for those associated with the form realm and the formless realm.

Regarding the latent dispositions (anuśaya) present in a mind of the past that is bound to the desire realm and abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*): if they do not increase (*anuśerate*) with respect to this mind, do they also not act as its cause?
If it does not act as a cause, does it also not increase accordingly?

And so on, up to: regarding all latent dispositions (anuśaya) associated with the present formless realm that are to be abandoned by cultivation, if they do not increase accordingly with respect to this mind, do they also not act as its cause?
If it does not act as a cause, does it also not increase accordingly?

Regarding all latent dispositions (anuśaya) associated with the past mind of the desire realm that is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), if they do not increase accordingly toward this mind, do they also not act as its cause?

Either it does not act as a cause but does not fail to increase [through association], or it does not increase [through association] but does not fail to act as a cause, or it neither acts as a cause nor increases [through association], or it neither fails to act as a cause nor fails to increase [through association].

Furthermore, regarding those that are not causes but do not fail to increase [in association], this refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) which, being of the same class and universal (sarvatraga), follow after this mind; that is, those very latent dispositions take this [mind] as their object and have not yet been abandoned.

Regarding that which is neither "increased by following" (*anuśerate*) nor "not acting as a cause": this refers to those proclivities (*anuśaya*) that, being of the same class or universal (*sarvatraga*), preceded this mind; specifically, those proclivities which do not take this [mind] as an object, or which, even if they did, have been abandoned, as well as the associated proclivities that have already been abandoned.

That which cannot serve as a cause and does not increase by way of being associated is as follows: regarding the various latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that are of the same class or are universal (*sarvatraga*) and arise after this mind—namely, those very latent dispositions—if they do not take this [mind] as their object; or even if they do take it as their object, they have already been abandoned; or if they are other objects; or if they are other latent dispositions; or if they are universal latent dispositions belonging to a different realm (*dhātu*).

"Not being non-causes and not being non-increasing" refers to those proclivities that, prior to this mind, are of the same class and are universal; that is, those very proclivities take this [mind] as their object and have not been abandoned, as well as the associated proclivities which have not been abandoned.
As it was with the mind associated with the desire realm to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*) in the past, so it is in the future.

Regarding the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) present in a mind associated with the desire realm to be abandoned by the vision of suffering in the present: if they do not increase (*anuśerate*) in this mind, do they also not act as its cause?

Either it does not act as a cause but does not fail to increase [through association], or it does not increase [through association] but does not fail to act as a cause, or it neither acts as a cause nor increases [through association], or it neither fails to act as a cause nor fails to increase [through association].

Furthermore, regarding that which does not act as a cause but is not non-increasing: this refers to those latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are of the same class and are pervasive (sarvatraga) in relation to this mind, and which have not yet been abandoned while taking this [mind] as their object.

Regarding "that which is neither an object of increase nor not a cause": it refers to those proclivities (anuśaya) that are of the same class and are pervasive (sarvatraga) prior to this mind; that is, those proclivities do not take this [mind] as their object, or if they did, they have already been abandoned.

That which cannot serve as a cause and is not an underlying tendency (*anuśaya*) refers to those underlying tendencies that follow this mind—namely, those of the same class or the universal (*sarvatraga*) types—which do not take this [mind] as their object; or, even if they do take it as an object, have already been abandoned; or, if they take other objects; or, if they are other underlying tendencies; or, if they are universal underlying tendencies belonging to a different realm (*dhātu*).

"Neither not acting as a cause nor not increasing [by way of association]" refers to those proclivities that precede this mind—namely, its homogeneous and universal proclivities—which have not yet been abandoned with respect to this [mind], as well as all proclivities associated with it.

As it is with the mind abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), so it is with the defiled minds abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).

Regarding the non-defiled minds belonging to the past that are connected to the desire realm and abandoned through cultivation, do all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that exist therein neither increase (*anuvardhate*) within this mind nor act as its cause?

This refers to all latent dispositions (anuśaya) present in other non-defiled minds of the desire realm that are to be abandoned by cultivation, excluding those resulting from the maturation (vipāka) of latent dispositions; these [dispositions], with respect to such a mind, either do not increase (na-anuśerate) therein and are not its cause, or they are not its cause but do increase therein—namely, those latent dispositions which take this mind as their object and have not yet been abandoned.

Regarding the maturation (vipāka) induced by the various proclivities (anuśaya), there are cases where it either does not act as a cause but does not fail to increase [the proclivity], or does not increase [the proclivity] but does not fail to act as a cause, or acts neither as a cause nor increases [the proclivity], or neither fails to act as a cause nor fails to increase [the proclivity].

That which cannot serve as a cause but does not fail to increase accordingly refers to those latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that do not act as causes for the maturation (*vipāka*) of this mind, yet those very same latent dispositions take this [mind] as their object and have not been abandoned.
