Either the object of focus (*ālambana*) is not yet severed while its substance (*svabhāva*) is also not yet severed; or the object of focus is not yet severed while its substance has already been severed; or both the object of focus and the object of focus [in another sense] are not yet severed while its substance is not yet severed; or both the object of focus and the object of focus have already been severed while its substance has already been severed.

Regarding those whose objects of perception (*ālambana*) have not been abandoned and whose essence has not been abandoned: this refers to individuals who are bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana-pudgala*). Their various wholesome minds (*kuśala-citta*) pertaining to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) take as their objects those pertaining to the desire realm, those pertaining to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), those pertaining to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), those pertaining to both the desire and form realms, those pertaining to both the desire and formless realms, those pertaining to both the form and formless realms, and those pertaining to all three realms simultaneously. Having not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, and with the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) not yet arisen, these various wholesome minds pertaining to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors abandoned by seeing cessation, by seeing the path, and by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire, then those wholesome minds bound to the realm of desire that take as their object states to be abandoned through cultivation are said to have their objects unsevered while their substance is also unsevered.

Regarding those whose objects of perception have not been abandoned while their own substance has already been abandoned: this refers to one who has already become detached from the greed of the desire realm but has not yet become detached from the greed of the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such a person’s various wholesome minds associated with the desire realm take as their objects those things associated with the form realm, those associated with the formless realm, or both those associated with the form and formless realms.

When one has already abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) but the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) take that which is bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) as their object.
This is called "that whose object is not yet severed, but whose substance is already severed."

Regarding those whose objects of cognition (*ālambana*) have not been abandoned, as well as those whose objects have already been abandoned but whose substance (*svabhāva*) has not yet been abandoned: this refers to wholesome minds bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; these minds take as their objects the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, then all wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by vision and cultivation.
This is called "the object is not abandoned and [the mind] is associated with that object."

Regarding those whose substance has been abandoned but whose objects have not been abandoned, or whose objects have been abandoned while their substance has also been abandoned: this refers to one who has already become detached from the greed of the desire realm but has not yet become detached from the greed of the form realm; for such a person, various wholesome minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects things bound to the desire realm and the form realm, things bound to the desire realm and the formless realm, or things bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

Having already abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) but not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), all wholesome minds (*kuśalacitta*) bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) take as their objects those things bound to the desire realm and the formless realm, those bound to the form realm and the formless realm, and those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.
This is called that whose object has not been abandoned and whose object has already been abandoned, yet whose substance is also abandoned.
Regarding those unwholesome minds whose substance has not been abandoned, is their object also not abandoned?

Either the entity is not yet abandoned while the object is also not yet abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has already been abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while both the object has already been abandoned and the object is also not yet abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned such that it is impossible to distinguish whether this mind’s object has been abandoned or not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose essence is not yet severed and whose objects are not yet severed: this refers to the unwholesome minds of individuals who are bound by all fetters, which take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm, that which is bound to the form realm, that which is bound to the formless realm, or that which is bound to both the form and formless realms.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds associated with views to be abandoned by the vision of origin take as their objects that which is to be abandoned by the vision of origin, cessation, the path, and that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.
All unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of the origin [of suffering] take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of the origin.
All unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of cessation take as their object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation.

All unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) take as their object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing. All unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*) take as their object that which is abandoned through the path of cultivation.

When the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of seeing cessation take as their object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing cessation.
All unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of seeing take as their object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing.
All unwholesome minds abandoned through cultivation take as their object that which is abandoned through cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the path of seeing take as their object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing.
All unwholesome minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned the greed of the desire realm, all unwholesome minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned but an object already abandoned: this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; [in such a state], unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of origin take as their objects those things abandoned through the vision of suffering.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned.

Regarding that which is "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned" as well as "the object is not yet abandoned": it refers to an unwholesome mind associated with views that is to be abandoned by seeing the origin (*samudaya-darśana-heya*), belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm (*kāma-avītarāga*), in whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such a mind takes as its objects those things to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
This is called "that whose essence is not yet abandoned, but whose object has been abandoned, as well as that whose object has not been abandoned.

Regarding those whose essence is not yet abandoned and for whom it is impossible to distinguish whether the object of this mind has been abandoned or not: this refers to the unwholesome minds of individuals who are bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana-pudgala*), which take as their objects that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

When the knowledge of origin has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, those unwholesome minds abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path (*darśana-nirodha-mārga-prahātavya*) take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned by the path of vision take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, and it cannot be distinguished whether the objects of this mind have been abandoned or not."
If the object of focus (*ālambana*) has not been abandoned, is its substance (*svabhāva*) also not abandoned?

There are four possibilities: either the object of focus has not been abandoned and its substance has not been abandoned; or the object of focus has not been abandoned but its substance has already been abandoned; or both the object of focus and the object of focus that has already been abandoned have their substance not yet abandoned; or both the object of focus and the object of focus that has already been abandoned have their substance already abandoned.

Regarding those whose objects of perception (*ālambana*) have not been abandoned and whose essential nature (*svabhāva*) has not been abandoned: this refers to the unwholesome minds of a person (*pudgala*) bound by all fetters, which take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), that which is bound to the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), that which is bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), or that which is bound to both the form and formless realms; who have not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm; and for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen—namely, the unwholesome minds to be abandoned by the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-heya*) which take as their objects [the truths of] origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
An unwholesome mind abandoned through the vision of the origin conditions objects abandoned through the vision of the origin;
an unwholesome mind abandoned through the vision of cessation conditions objects abandoned through the vision of cessation;
an unwholesome mind abandoned through the vision of the path conditions objects abandoned through the vision of the path.
Unwholesome minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, unwholesome minds to be abandoned by the vision of cessation take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Unwholesome minds abandoned by the path of seeing take as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing.
Unwholesome minds abandoned by cultivation take as their object that which is abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned by the path of seeing take as their object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing.
All unwholesome minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their objects those things to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of sensuality, all unwholesome minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their objects those things to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the object of cognition is not abandoned and its substance is not abandoned.

Regarding "the object of cognition is not abandoned but its substance is already abandoned": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, whose knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen but whose knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; their unwholesome minds to be abandoned by seeing suffering take as their objects those things to be abandoned by seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination take as their object that which is to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, as well as that which is to be abandoned through cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination take as their object that which is to be abandoned through the vision of the path and that which is to be abandoned through cultivation.

If one considers a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm: their unwholesome minds to be abandoned by insight take as objects those things to be abandoned by cultivation.

If they have already abandoned craving for the desire realm but have not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen: their unwholesome minds take as objects those things bound to the form realm, those bound to the formless realm, or those bound to both the form and formless realms.

When one has already abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) but the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds take the objects belonging to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).
This is called "the object of perception is not yet severed, while its substance is already severed."

Regarding those whose objects of cognition (*ālambana*) are both not yet abandoned and already abandoned, while their own substance (*svabhāva*) is not yet abandoned: this refers to one who has not yet abandoned the craving of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; [in such a state], all unwholesome minds (*akuśala-citta*) abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) take as their objects those things abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).
This is called: "the object of cognition is not yet abandoned, and although the object has been abandoned, its substance is not yet abandoned";

and "the object of cognition is not yet abandoned, and although the object has been abandoned, its substance has already been abandoned. Regarding the latter: it refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), in whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; their unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering take as their objects those things abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination take as their objects that which is to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as that which is to be abandoned through cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unwholesome minds abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin take as their objects the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation.

If one sees a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected [right] view but has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, their unwholesome minds abandoned through seeing take as objects those [factors] abandoned through seeing and cultivation.

If they have already abandoned craving for the form realm but have not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, their unwholesome minds take as objects those factors bound to the form realm and the formless realm.
This is called "the object of focus is not yet abandoned, and its substance is already abandoned.
Regarding those obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm: if their substance is not yet abandoned, is their object of focus also not yet abandoned?
He said: "It is so. If that which is the object-condition has not been abandoned, is its substance also not abandoned?"

Either the object of perception (*ālambana*) is not yet severed while its substance (*svabhāva*) is also not yet severed; or the object of perception is not yet severed while its substance has already been severed; or both the object of perception and its substance have already been severed.

Regarding those whose objects of perception have not been severed and whose essence has not been severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm that take as their object things bound to the desire realm, belonging to individuals who are still bound by all fetters.
This is called "the object of cognition is not abandoned and its substance is not abandoned.

Regarding "the object of cognition is not abandoned but its substance is already abandoned": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, in whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; [in such a person], the obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds associated with the desire realm that are to be abandoned by seeing suffering take as their objects those things to be abandoned by seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds of the desire realm associated with the vision of suffering take as their objects that which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, as well as that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm that are to be abandoned by seeing suffering take as their objects both what is to be abandoned by seeing the path and what is to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire, then all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the realm of desire take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the object of cognition has not been abandoned, but its substance has already been abandoned.

Regarding "the object of cognition has not been abandoned, and the object of cognition has been abandoned, while its substance has already been abandoned": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned the craving of the desire realm, for whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; their various obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned through cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire, their various obscured-unspecified minds bound to the realm of desire take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation.
This is called "that whose object is not yet abandoned and whose object is already abandoned, while its own substance is already abandoned.
Regarding those unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm, if their substance is not yet abandoned, is their object also not yet abandoned?

Either the entity is not yet abandoned while the object is also not yet abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has already been abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while both the object has already been abandoned and the object is also not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose substance is not yet severed and whose objects are not yet severed: this refers to individuals who are bound by all fetters; their various non-obscured, neutral minds associated with the desire realm that take as their object the desire realm; they have not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm; the knowledge of suffering has already arisen, but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen; and their various non-obscured, neutral minds associated with the desire realm take as their objects those things to be abandoned through seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation.

When the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral (*anivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing the path and those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If one sees that a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision, but has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, possesses various unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm that take as their object what is to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned but an object already abandoned: it refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm, in whom the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; their various unobscured-neutral (*anivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those things to be abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering and origination.

When the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origination, and cessation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned the craving of the desire realm, their various unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by seeing.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned.

Regarding that which is "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned" as well as "the object is not yet abandoned": it refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the desire realm; when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, any unobscured-neutral mind (*anivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the desire realm that takes as its object the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the desire realm take as their objects those factors abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those abandoned through cultivation.

If one sees that a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision, but has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of desire, possesses various unobscured-neutral minds bound to the realm of desire that take as their objects those things to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object of perception is already abandoned, and the object of perception is not yet abandoned.
Now, if the object of perception is not yet abandoned, is its entity also not yet abandoned?
He replied:
Thus it is said.
*The Saṃyukta-abhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, Fascicle Seven.
*The Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra*, Fascicle Eight.
Composed by the Arhat Devaśarman;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Order. Section Three:

The Fourth Aggregate on the Object-condition (ālambana-pratyaya), Verse Summary (uddāna). Regarding all wholesome minds bound to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu-vītarāga*), if their substance is not yet severed, is their object also not yet severed?

Either its substance is not yet abandoned while its object is not yet abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned while its object has already been abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned while its object has both already been abandoned and not yet abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned and it is impossible to distinguish whether this mind’s object has been abandoned or not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose substance is not yet severed and whose objects are not yet severed: this refers to the wholesome minds of persons bound by all fetters that are connected to the form realm, which take as their objects those things connected to the desire realm, those connected to the form realm, those connected to the formless realm; those connected to both the desire and form realms; those connected to both the desire and formless realms; those connected to both the form and formless realms; and those connected to all three—the desire, form, and formless realms.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects things associated with the form realm, things associated with the formless realm, or things associated with both the form and formless realms.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the realm of form take as their objects those states to be abandoned by the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm (rūpāvacara) take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (bhāvanā-heya).

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by the vision of the path and those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, then those wholesome minds bound to the realm of form that take as their object what is to be abandoned by cultivation—
this is called "the entity is not abandoned and the object is not abandoned."

Regarding those whose substance has not been severed but whose objects have already been severed: this refers to one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such wholesome minds bound to the form realm take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the realm of form take as their object that which is to be abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudayānvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpāvacara*) take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering and origin.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, then those wholesome minds associated with the realm of form that take as their object what is to be abandoned by seeing—
this is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, while the object has already been abandoned."

Regarding those whose essence is not yet severed, but whose objects of perception (*ālambana*) are already severed, or whose objects of perception are not yet severed: this refers to wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) belonging to one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm; such minds take as their objects those things bound to the desire realm and the form realm, those bound to the desire realm and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), or those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudayānvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpāvacara*) take as their objects those factors to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If one observes a perfected disciple of the World-Honored One who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, their wholesome minds bound to the realm of form take as their objects those states to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object is already abandoned, and the object is also not yet abandoned."

Regarding the statement that "its substance has not been severed, yet it cannot be distinguished whether the object of this mind has been severed or not severed": this refers to the wholesome minds associated with the form realm belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters; these minds take as their objects that which is not to be severed.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the realm of form take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaye ’nvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpāvacara*) take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārge ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

If one sees that a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, then those wholesome minds bound to the realm of form take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, and it cannot be distinguished whether the objects of this mind have been abandoned or not."
If the object of focus (*ālambana*) has not been abandoned, is its substance (*svabhāva*) also not abandoned?

There are four possibilities: either the object has not been abandoned and its substance has not been abandoned; or the object has not been abandoned but its substance has already been abandoned; or both the object and its object have not been abandoned while its substance has not been abandoned; or both the object and its object have been abandoned while its substance has already been abandoned.

Regarding those whose objects of perception (*ālambana*) have not been severed and whose essential nature (*svabhāva*) has not been severed: this refers to all *pudgalas* bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana*), whose wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) take as their objects those associated with the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*), those associated with the form realm, those associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*); those associated with both the desire and form realms; those associated with both the desire and formless realms; those associated with both the form and formless realms; and those associated with the desire, form, and formless realms.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, before the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the form realm take as their objects that which is bound to the form realm, that which is bound to the formless realm, and that which is bound to both the form and formless realms.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the realm of form take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the knowledge of the category of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the category of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the knowledge of the category of the path has already arisen but [the subsequent knowledge] has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing the path and those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, then those wholesome minds bound to the realm of form that take as their object states to be abandoned through cultivation—
this is called "the object is not abandoned and its substance is not abandoned."

Regarding those whose objects of perception have not been abandoned while their own substance has already been abandoned: this refers to wholesome minds bound to the form realm that take the formless realm as their object, in one who has already become detached from the greed of the form realm but for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen.
This is called that whose object of cognition (*ālambana*) is not yet abandoned while its substance (*svabhāva*) has already been abandoned.

Regarding that whose object of cognition is not yet abandoned and whose object of cognition has already been abandoned while its substance has not yet been abandoned: this refers to wholesome minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) belonging to one who is already free from craving for the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) but not yet free from craving for the form realm; such minds take as their objects those things bound to the desire realm and the form realm, those bound to the desire realm and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), or those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds bound to the form realm take as their objects those states to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors belonging to the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned desire for the realm of form, then those wholesome minds bound to the realm of form that take as their object states to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation are said to have objects that are both not yet abandoned and already abandoned, while their own substance remains unabandoned.

Regarding those whose objects are not yet abandoned and those whose objects have been abandoned but whose essence has already been abandoned: this refers to wholesome minds bound to the form realm belonging to one who has already become detached from the greed of the form realm but has not yet become detached from the greed of the formless realm; such minds take as their objects that which is bound to the desire realm and the formless realm, that which is bound to the form realm and the formless realm, and that which is bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.
This is called "the object-condition is not yet severed, and its substance is already severed.
Regarding those minds associated with the form realm that are obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*): if their substance is not yet severed, is their object-condition also not yet severed?

Either its substance is not yet abandoned and its object is not yet abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned and its object has already been abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned and both its object has already been abandoned and its object is not yet abandoned; or its substance is not yet abandoned and it cannot be distinguished whether this mind’s object has been abandoned or not abandoned.

Regarding those whose intrinsic nature is not yet severed and whose objects of perception are not yet severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters, which take as their objects those things associated with the form realm, those associated with the formless realm, or both those associated with the form realm and the formless realm.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the form realm take as their objects that which is bound to the form realm, that which is bound to the formless realm, and that which is bound to both the form and formless realms.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the form realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of origination; these take as their objects the truths of origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
The obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through the vision of the origin conditions that which is abandoned through the vision of the origin;
the obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through the vision of cessation conditions that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation and that which is abandoned through the path of vision.
The obscured-unspecified mind has as its object that which is to be abandoned by the path of seeing.
The obscured-unspecified mind to be abandoned by cultivation has as its object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (samudaya-anvaya-jñāna) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, the obscured-unspecified minds of the form realm associated with the abandonment of the cessation of views have as their object that which is to be abandoned by the cessation of views.
The obscured-unspecified mind abandoned by the path of seeing takes as its object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing;
the obscured-unspecified mind abandoned by cultivation takes as its object that which is abandoned by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛtacitta*) belonging to the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśanamārga*) take as their object those [defilements] to be abandoned by the path of seeing.
The obscured-unspecified mind (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) takes that which is to be abandoned by cultivation as its object.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision (*dṛṣṭi-paripūrṇa*) has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), then all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the realm of form that are to be abandoned by cultivation take that which is to be abandoned by cultivation as their object.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned but an object already abandoned: it refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhajñāna-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudayajñāna-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; in such a person, any obscured-unspecified mind (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the realm of form that is to be abandoned by the vision of origination takes as its object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned.

Regarding that which is "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned" as well as "the object is not yet abandoned": it refers to the obscured-unspecified mind associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) that is to be abandoned by the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-heya*), belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such a mind takes as its objects those things to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, while the object is either already abandoned or not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which is "the entity is not yet abandoned and it is impossible to distinguish whether the object of this mind is already abandoned or not yet abandoned," this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm belonging to persons who are bound by all fetters, which take as their objects that which is not to be abandoned.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified (*nivṛta-avyākṛta*) minds bound to the form realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds bound to the realm of form take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds of the form realm associated with the views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (nirodha-anvaya-jñāna) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) belonging to the form realm (rūpadhātu) that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing (darśanamārga-prahātavya) take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (aprahātavya).
This is called "the substance is not yet severed, and it cannot be distinguished whether the object of this mind has been severed or not.
Furthermore, if the object is not yet severed, is its substance also not yet severed?

Either the object of cognition (*ālambana*) is not abandoned while its substance (*svabhāva*) is not abandoned; or the object of cognition is not abandoned while its substance has already been abandoned; or both the object of cognition is not abandoned and the object of cognition has already been abandoned while its substance is not abandoned; or both the object of cognition is not abandoned and the object of cognition has already been abandoned while its substance has already been abandoned.

Regarding those whose objects of perception (*ālambana*) have not been abandoned and whose essence has not been abandoned: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana-pudgala*), which take as their objects that which is associated with the form realm, that which is associated with the formless realm, or that which is associated with both the form and formless realms.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) bound to the form realm take as their objects that which is bound to the form realm, that which is bound to the formless realm, or that which is bound to both the form and formless realms.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the form realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of origin; these take as their objects the truths of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation.
The obscured-neutral mind abandoned through the vision of the origin has as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of the origin;
the obscured-neutral mind abandoned through the vision of cessation has as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation.
The obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through the path of seeing takes as its object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing;
the obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through cultivation takes as its object that which is abandoned through cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation.
The obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through the path of seeing takes as its object that which is abandoned through the path of seeing;
the obscured-unspecified mind abandoned through cultivation takes as its object that which is abandoned through cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*) has already arisen, but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛtacitta*) bound to the form realm that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing, which take as their object those [states] to be abandoned by the path of seeing.
The obscured-unspecified mind (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) to be abandoned by cultivation takes as its object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned attachment to the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), then their various form-realm-bound obscured-unspecified minds to be abandoned by cultivation take as their objects that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the object of cognition is not abandoned and its substance is not abandoned.

Regarding "the object of cognition is not abandoned but its substance is already abandoned": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; their obscured-unspecified (*nivṛta-avyākṛta*) minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering take as their objects those states to be abandoned by the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified (*nivṛtāvyākṛta*) minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin take as their objects those states to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds of the form realm associated with the views to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the seeing of origination take as their object the path to be seen and that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, their obscured-unspecified mind associated with the form realm—which is to be abandoned by insight—takes as its object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.

One who has already abandoned craving for the form realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, possesses all obscured-unspecified minds (nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta) bound to the form realm that take as their object that which is bound to the formless realm.
This is called "that whose object has not been abandoned but whose essence has already been abandoned.

Regarding "that whose object has not been abandoned and that whose object has been abandoned but whose essence has not been abandoned": this refers to an obscured-unspecified mind (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), which is to be abandoned by the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-heya*), belonging to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; such a mind takes as its objects those things to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
This is called "the object of cognition is not yet abandoned, and although the object of cognition has been abandoned, its substance is not yet abandoned.

Regarding "the object of cognition is not yet abandoned, and although the object of cognition has been abandoned, its substance is already abandoned": this refers to one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), in whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; [in such a person], all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the realm of form that are to be abandoned by seeing suffering, and which take as their objects the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛta-avyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm (*rūpa-dhātu*) that are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin take as their objects [the truths of] suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvayajñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has not yet arisen, there are obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛtacitta*) associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering and its origin; these take as their objects the truths of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāheya*).

If one considers a perfected disciple of the Blessed One who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, their obscured-unspecified minds associated with the form realm that are to be abandoned by insight take as their objects those things to be abandoned by both insight and cultivation.

For one who has already abandoned craving for the form realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, all obscured-unspecified minds bound to the form realm take as their objects those things bound to the form realm and the formless realm.
This is called that whose object has not been abandoned and whose object has been abandoned, yet whose substance has already been abandoned.

Regarding those unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu-pratisaṃyukta-anivṛtāvyākṛtacitta*), if their substance has not been abandoned, has their object also not been abandoned?

Either the entity is not yet abandoned while the object is not yet abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has already been abandoned; or the entity is not yet abandoned while both the object has already been abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose essence is not yet severed and whose objects are not yet severed: this refers to the unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters, which take as their objects that which is associated with the desire realm or associated with the form realm.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the form realm take as their object that which is bound to the form realm.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds (*anivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) bound to the form realm take as their objects those [defilements] to be abandoned by seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origination has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those states to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those states to be abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, then all unobscured-neutral minds bound to the realm of form take as their object that which is to be abandoned by cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned but an object already abandoned: it refers to the various unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) that take objects belonging to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), in the case of one who has already become detached from the greed of the desire realm but has not yet become detached from the greed of the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkhe ’nvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

For one who has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds (*anivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the realm of form take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds (*anivṛta-avyākṛta-citta*) associated with the form realm take as their object those factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering and origin.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm take as their object those factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, their various unobscured-neutral minds associated with the realm of form take as their object that which is to be abandoned by vision.
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned.

Regarding that which is "the entity is not yet abandoned while the object has been abandoned" as well as "the object is not yet abandoned": it refers to the unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) for one who has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; these minds take as their objects those factors belonging to the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned through cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all unobscured-neutral minds associated with the form realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the realm of form, their various unobscured-neutral minds associated with the realm of form take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation.
This is called "the entity is not yet severed while the object-condition has been severed, and the object-condition is not yet severed.
Now, if the object-condition is not yet severed, is its entity also not yet severed?
He replied:
It is so. Regarding wholesome minds bound to the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), if their substance has not been abandoned, have their objects (*ālambana*) also not been abandoned?

There are cases where both the substance and the object have not been abandoned; cases where the substance has not been abandoned but the object has already been abandoned; cases where the substance has not been abandoned and both the object has already been abandoned and the object has not been abandoned; and cases where the substance has not been abandoned, yet it cannot be distinguished whether the object of this mind has been abandoned or not abandoned.

Regarding those whose essence is not yet severed and whose objects are not yet severed: this refers to the wholesome minds associated with the formless realm belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters, which take as their objects those things associated with the form realm or those associated with the formless realm.

Having already become detached from the craving of the desire realm, but not yet having become detached from the craving of the form realm, while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their objects those things associated with the form realm or those associated with the formless realm.

For one who has already abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) but for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) take as their object that which is associated with the formless realm.

For one for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object those things to be abandoned by seeing origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudayānvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodhānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of the path and by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, then those wholesome minds associated with the formless realm that take as their object states to be abandoned through cultivation—
this is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned."

Regarding those whose substance has not been severed but whose objects have already been severed: this refers to wholesome minds associated with the formless realm that take as their object the form realm, belonging to one who has already abandoned craving for the form realm but for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

When the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpya-dhātu*) take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is to be abandoned by the vision of suffering and origin.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārga-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpya-dhātu-pratisaṃyukta*) take as their objects those [defilements] to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation.

If it is a disciple of the Blessed One who is perfected in vision (*dṛṣṭi-sampanna*), but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, then all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their objects those [defilements] to be abandoned by vision (*darśana-heya*).
This is called "the entity is not yet abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an entity not yet abandoned and an object already abandoned, as well as an object not yet abandoned: this refers to wholesome minds bound to the formless realm when the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origination (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen; these minds take as their objects the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, as well as those factors to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their objects those factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, as well as those to be abandoned by cultivation.

If a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, their various wholesome minds bound to the formless realm take as their objects those states to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation.
This is called "that whose essence is not yet abandoned, while its object is either already abandoned or not yet abandoned.

Regarding that which has an essence not yet abandoned for which it is impossible to distinguish whether the object of this mind is already abandoned or not yet abandoned: this refers to the wholesome minds associated with the formless realm belonging to a person who is bound by all fetters, which take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

For one who has already abandoned craving for the desire realm but has not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, and for whom the subsequent knowledge of suffering (duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

When one has already become detached from the greed of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) but the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) take as their object that which is not to be abandoned (*aprahātavya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

When the subsequent knowledge of origin has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

When the subsequent knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the subsequent knowledge of the path has not yet arisen, all wholesome minds associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is not to be abandoned.

If one sees that a disciple of the Blessed One who has perfected vision, but has not yet abandoned craving for the formless realm, possesses wholesome minds bound to the formless realm that take as their object that which is not to be abandoned—
this is called "the entity is not yet abandoned, and it cannot be distinguished whether the objects of this mind have been abandoned or not."
If the object of focus has not been abandoned, has its substance also not been abandoned?
It is said: Yes.

Regarding all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*): if their substance is not yet abandoned, is their object (*ālambana*) also not yet abandoned?

There are four possibilities: (1) the substance is not yet abandoned and the object is also not yet abandoned; (2) the substance is not yet abandoned but the object is already abandoned; (3) the substance is not yet abandoned and both the object is already abandoned and the object is not yet abandoned; (4) the substance is not yet abandoned, and it is impossible to distinguish whether this mind’s object is already abandoned or not yet abandoned.

Regarding those whose essence is not severed and whose objects are not severed: this refers to the obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that take as their objects things associated with the formless realm, belonging to individuals who are bound by all fetters.

Having already abandoned craving for the desire realm but not yet abandoned craving for the form realm, while the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is associated with the formless realm.

Having already abandoned craving for the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), but before the subsequent knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds (*nivṛtāvyākṛta-citta*) associated with the formless realm take as their object that which is associated with the formless realm.

Once the subsequent knowledge of suffering has arisen, but before the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen, all obscured-unspecified minds associated with the formless realm that are to be abandoned by the vision of origin take as their object those things to be abandoned by the vision of origin, cessation, the path, and by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
The obscured-neutral mind abandoned through the vision of the origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) takes as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of the origin.
The obscured-neutral mind abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya) takes as its object that which is abandoned through the vision of cessation.
The obscured-neutral mind abandoned by the path of seeing takes as its object that which is abandoned by the path of seeing;
the obscured-neutral mind abandoned by the path of cultivation takes as its object that which is abandoned by the path of cultivation.
